niche: a New Zealand lines company's zone-substation transformer fleet, choosing which three transformers get the 2027/28 internal inspection outages from five years of dissolved gas analysis
answer: Southbridge T2, Rolleston T2 and Coalgate T1 (SBG-T2 8.07, RLS-T2 4.98, CGT-T1 4.73), in that order

stakeholder_role: network asset manager at a lines company, who takes the inspection slate to the board with the 2027/28 capital works programme

spine.entity: one laboratory dissolved gas analysis of one main-tank oil sample from one transformer

world.org_type: electricity distribution business (lines company) with 44 zone-substation power transformers

driver: A monitored signal that the standard reads as the unit's own fault can be carried in from an attached compartment whose ordinary operation produces it, so ranking units on the signal measured in the main body puts units with a leaking neighbour ahead of units with genuine internal faults; only attributing each unit's signal to its source, by its co-movement with the neighbour's operations and its composition, separates them.
driver_concrete: Acetylene in a transformer's main-tank oil reads as arcing and the fleet DGA standard codes it most severely; at two zone substations with in-oil arcing tap changers (Dunsandel T1 and Leeston T2) the barrier between the tap-changer compartment and the main tank weeps, so their main-tank acetylene rises with every tap change (r 0.998 and 0.995, twelve-month C2H2/H2 9.8 and 8.2) and their code-3 severities lead the fleet (9.64 and 8.07), while Southbridge T2, with a vacuum tap changer, carries the same acetylene (8.07) from a genuine internal arc; a slate built on main-tank codes spends two of its three outages on tap-changer seals.
stump: A competent solver codes every transformer under ES-DGA-02 from its main-tank samples (limits by preservation type and age, twelve-month increases, code 3 ranked by severity) and names Dunsandel T1 (9.64), Leeston T2 (8.07) and Southbridge T2 (8.07), two of which carry acetylene leaked from in-oil tap-changer compartments; the step that lands it there is reading main-tank acetylene as a main-tank fault, when at Dunsandel T1 and Leeston T2 its increments track the tap-change counts (r 0.998 and 0.995) and its twelve-month ratio to hydrogen is 9.8 and 8.2. A solver who does attribute, but by the counter alone, drops Rolleston T2 as well (its acetylene tracks its counter at r 0.999, arc gas from the tap selector in the main-tank oil, C2H2/H2 0.64) and names Southbridge T2, Coalgate T1 and Springston T2. The slate takes the vacuum-tap-changer unit with the same acetylene (Southbridge T2), the in-oil unit whose acetylene is made in its main tank (Rolleston T2, 4.98) and the worst thermal fault (Coalgate T1, 4.73).

lineage.architecture: v1 (screen grain: metering system against supply number)
lineage.fate: spent at in-house solver round 1 (2026-10-11): plain 81.3 and skeptic 85.6, both landed Caithness 54; the filed glossary and the related metering points sheet made the grain a work order
lineage.driver: The referral test is filed for each metered sub-unit against its own history, but the ready-made series sums the sub-units of an entity, and where an entity holds a second sub-unit carrying one seasonal load, a large fall on that sub-unit moves the entity total by a few per cent, inside ordinary variation, so screening the summed series ranks the candidates differently from screening each sub-unit and counting entities once.

notes: Re-root of task180 (architecture 2). Subdomain asset-condition-maintenance carried under Anomaly Detection & Diagnostics because DGA interpretation is fault diagnosis on condition-monitoring anomalies. Bespoke draw from how zone-substation transformers are built (in-oil arcing tap changers in a compartment sharing a barrier with the main tank on older units, vacuum tap changers on newer ones) and monitored (main-tank DGA on a schedule, compartment samples less often, tap-change counters on SCADA). No calibration corpus, no licensed wrong basis; the fleet DGA standard is filed in full and says nothing about compartment leakage. Hardening loop 1 (round 2 landed by tap-counter attribution): Rolleston T2's arc is at the tap selector in the main-tank oil, so its acetylene tracks its counter like the leaks' and only the gas it arrives with (C2H2/H2) keeps it on the slate. Stump strategy relabelled from stated_rule_hard_construction to decomposition_attribution at hardening loop 1 under the client's three rules (2026-10-10): what decides is splitting the main-tank acetylene between two sources whose tracking overlaps, not building a filed quantity. Hardening loop 2 (round 4 landed on the plain gas ratio): Leeston T2's new galvanised radiators give off hydrogen from before its first acetylene, so only the hydrogen the acetylene brings of its own separates the leaks from Rolleston T2.
layer1: laboratory DGA reports with sampling and analysis dates, below-detection values written as <n, O2 and N2 for the preservation type, corrected reports re-issued under the same sample ID, and a label oil temperature sometimes left blank
an asset register with rewind years, tap-changer types by make and model, and a last-service field not written back since March 2025
SCADA daily tap-change counters that roll over at 99,999 and restart at zero when a counter is replaced at a tap-changer service
a historian export of hourly top-oil temperature and load with UTC timestamps and no zone marker
a maintenance log in free text with tap-changer services, oil processing and breather changes
a mobile substation booking schedule for the 2027/28 outages
analyst_test: A strong analyst who keeps the latest issue of every report, codes all 44 transformers correctly under ES-DGA-02 and reads 5.1 and 5.2 as giving the outages only to faults in the main tank still takes an easy attribution: dropping every transformer whose acetylene rises in step with its tap operations files Southbridge T2, Coalgate T1 and Springston T2 (Rolleston T2's acetylene tracks its counter too, but brings hydrogen of its own), and reading the plain gas ratio keeps Leeston T2, whose hydrogen is its new galvanised radiators', rising for months before its first acetylene.
domain_test: What decides the slate is a dissolved-gas diagnosis of where each transformer's main-tank acetylene was generated, diverter-compartment oil carried through a weeping barrier (C2H2/H2 of 8 to 10) against an arc in the main-tank oil (more hydrogen than acetylene), which is the field's own fault-gas interpretation (IEC 60599); with schools or clinics in place of transformers there is no gas, tap changer or ratio to read, so the task does not survive the swap.
